items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the arts and cultural affairs law, in relation to establishing the Edward Hopper citation of merit for visual artists
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S4235

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the arts and cultural affairs law, in
relation to establishing the Edward Hopper citation of merit for
visual artists

PURPOSE:

This legislation would establish the New York State Edward Hopper
citation of merit to be awarded biennially.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

This legislation establishes the Edward Hopper Citation of Merit. The
recipient of this citation shall be a New York State visual artist who
is making a significant contribution to the advancement of the arts in
New York. An advisory panel, appointed by the NYS Arts Council, shall
biennially choose the recipient. The recipient shall promote and
encourage the visual arts give at least two showings in the State each
year, one of which shall be held at the Edward Hopper House in Nyack,
NY.

JUSTIFICATION:

As with the Walt Whitman citation of merit for poetry and the Edith
Wharton citation of merit for fiction writers, the Edward Hopper
citation of merit for visual artists will showcase the vast talent
that New York State has to offer. The arts have always been an
integral part of New York State. By recognizing visual artists who
make a significant contribution, New York will continue to grow its
ever present and culturally diverse artist's communities.

New York State history is rich with artists that have called the State
home, in particular, Edward Hopper. Edward Hopper was born in the
Village of Nyack in 1882 and lived in New York State all of his life.
He achieved great success as an artist worldwide - participating in
exhibits at major museums and gracing the cover of Time magazine.
Hopper is most iconic paintings are set in New York and include
Nighthawks, Room in New York, From Williamsburg Bridge and Early
Sunday Morning. His popularity has increased around the world in
recent years. In the summer of 2014, The Art Everywhere US project
allowed people throughout the US to vote for the works of American art
they most wanted to see in public displays around the country.  The
artwork that received the most votes was Hopper's Nighthawks. The
Edward Hopper House (the artist's childhood home in Nyack, NY)
regularly welcomes visitors from around that world.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

$10,000 honorarium biennially ($5,000 per year).

EFFECTIVE DATE:


Immediately.
